slices.focus: A severe voice flare forces Colleen to stop treating hoarseness as a minor annoyance and adopt real preventive measures.
slices.summary: After a day of stacked spring tours plus outreach, Colleen's voice drops out badly enough to send her to urgent care. The clinician tells her this is cumulative, not occasional. She adopts a microphone, stricter water tracking, and begins limiting consecutive high-talk days. She also cuts back some freelance walking-tour weekends for recovery. Starts reframing voice protection as 'equipment, not concession.'
open_loops: Scheduling conversation with work about pacing -- waiting until habits are established first
Mic adoption needs to become default, not optional
Threshold rule needed for consecutive high-talk days
